extracted.intended_audience: researchers studying peer review and research funding; funding agencies and programme officers; grant reviewers; early-career researchers learning to write or review proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Systematic-review synthesis and conceptualization of the evaluation criteria peers use when assessing grant proposals, identifying 15 evaluation criteria and their associations with evaluated entities (applicant, project, environment), and grouping them into aims, means, and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality — the novelty or innovativeness of the proposed research. Originality was the only criterion which appeared in all included studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used primarily to assess the aims and outcomes of a proposal (research question, topic, results). Appears as a core epistemic value in the conceptualization (purple community). Exclusive to project-level assessment in the reviewed studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic relevance — the contribution of the proposal to academic knowledge and scholarly discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used mainly to evaluate the aims and expected results (academic significance). Reported in multiple studies (8 studies). Part of the 'relevance' family alongside extra-academic and general relevance; associated with the purple community in the bipartite network.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra-academic (non-academic) relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Extra-academic relevance — the societal, practical or non-academic benefits and consequences of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the most frequent criteria (14% of assigned codes). Used to assess aims/outcomes and potential impacts; grouped with originality and academic relevance as key dimensions of research quality in peer review (purple community).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness — the fit or suitability of methods, design, or other proposal components for achieving the aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the research-process evaluation cluster (green community); used to assess methodological choices on the content level. Notably, appropriateness was one of the criteria used to evaluate all three main entities (applicant, project, environment) in the included studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Completeness — the extent to which the proposal and applicant information are fully reported and include necessary details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A descriptive-level quality criterion (part of 'quality of description'), accounting for ~13% of criterion codes. Used to evaluate how well the proposed project and applicant information are described; connected with clarity in assessing the descriptive sufficiency of the research plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity — how clearly the proposal, methods, and arguments are presented and communicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A descriptive-level criterion (part of 'quality of description'), ~10% frequency. Evaluates readability and explicitness of the proposal; used mainly in assessing the research process and how it is reported (green community).

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Feasibility — the plausibility that the project can be implemented with the proposed resources, timeline, and personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the six most frequent criteria (~10%). Central to the orange community: links applicant qualifications, resources (budget, environment), and project plan. Used to assess project resources and (according to the review) was one of the few criteria applied to all three main entities (applicant, project, environment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Rigor — the methodological soundness and thoroughness of the proposed research approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A content-level research-process criterion (grouped with appropriateness, coherence/justification, and quality). Used primarily to assess entities related to the research process (theory, data, method, analysis); treated as part of research quality in the conceptualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence/justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Coherence/justification — the logical consistency of the proposal and how well choices and claims are justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether the research plan and arguments fit together and are well supported. Part of the research-process cluster (green community) and considered a content-level indicator of plausibility/soundness alongside appropriateness and rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality — a general assessment of the merit or overall standard of elements of the proposal (often used in less granular terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as a general criterion (blue community) for assessing method in general or the research process at a higher abstraction level. Less specific than rigor/appropriateness/coherence; used to evaluate research process entities in broader terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Motivation — the applicant’s drive, commitment, or purpose for pursuing the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified under 'personal qualities' and part of the red community (psychological perspective). In the reviewed studies motivation was used exclusively to assess the applicant (applicant in general).

rubrics_metrics.name: Traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Traits — personal characteristics or attributes of the applicant (e.g., temperament, reliability, other dispositional features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also part of 'personal qualities' (red community). Like motivation, traits were reported only in relation to applicant assessment (exclusive to applicant-level evaluation in the included studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversity — sociological attributes or demographic/identity-related considerations relevant to the applicant or team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears in the red community as a sociological perspective on the applicant/personality. The review notes that diversity (together with appropriateness and feasibility) was one of the criteria used to assess all three main entities in some studies; it captures social/representational considerations rather than purely epistemic ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: General relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: General relevance — a broadly defined notion of the proposal’s importance or pertinence (less specifically labelled than academic or extra-academic relevance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defined in more general terms in the qualitative coding and occurred rarely (~4% of assigned codes). Treated as a high-level relevance indicator when authors report criteria at coarser abstraction levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other (residual category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other — a residual category indicating additional evaluation criteria reported in included studies that are not enumerated in the main list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included to capture occasional or study-specific criteria not captured by the 14 named categories; the review notes that some studies reported entities and criteria beyond the ones summarized and that 'other' entries exist both for entities and criteria.
